problem.name: Partition-function estimation
problem.statement_latex:
Given an energy $H:\Omega\to\{0,\ldots,B\}$ and inverse temperature $\beta$, output $\widehat Z$ with $|\widehat Z/Z-1|\le\varepsilon$, where $Z(\beta)=\sum_{x\in\Omega}e^{-\beta H(x)}$. Suitable choices count independent sets, matchings and colorings; the zero-temperature limit counts optimal configurations.
Complexity counts coherent or classical Markov-chain steps and energy evaluations, with arithmetic costs restored for numerical output.

quantum.details_latex: Here $\delta$ bounds the spectral gaps of the supplied sampling chains. Montanaro\textquotesingle s estimator uses $\widetilde O(\ell^2/(\varepsilon\sqrt\delta))$ for a supplied length-$\ell$ constant-relative-variance cooling schedule. In the independent-set uniqueness regime, appropriate Glauber dynamics yield a representative $\widetilde O(n^{5/4}/\varepsilon)$ bound. Schedule preparation and initial-state assumptions are part of these theorems.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(\log|\Omega|/(\varepsilon^2\delta))$, \v Stefankovi\v c--Vempala--Vigoda adaptive cooling and classical sampling.
classical.headline_text: $\widetilde O(\log|\Omega|/(\varepsilon^2\delta))$, Štefankovič–Vempala–Vigoda adaptive cooling and classical sampling.
classical.details_latex: For explicit sparse graphs, independent-set, fixed-$q$ coloring and perfect-matching counts also admit exact $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time through sparse Boolean counting. For sparse constant-arity, constant-bit integer energies, counting each of the $O(n)$ possible energies gives the density of states and hence $Z$ with that exponent, plus numerical precision costs. These exact methods are useful when the supplied chain mixes slowly; in uniqueness regimes, polynomial-time correlation-decay and sampling algorithms provide classical alternatives.

hardware.description_latex: A configuration on $n$ bits needs at least $n$ logical data qubits, plus reversible transition, energy and estimation workspace. Fault tolerance and coherent Markov-chain steps are required; depth depends on $\delta^{-1/2}$.
